notes: Runs: all five have rc 0, head ba24972 with uncommitted false; git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ is empty, so the rules graded are the text the runs were given (the baseline runs read none of it). result.json skills_listed is 29 for every run. None of the sessions ran mix format.

Same standard as evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/macro-dsl-baseline.json and macro-dsl-skill.json for unchanged rules: git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ leaves macros.md and library-design.md untouched, so the seven macro and library rules are graded as before. A route recorded by a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, while validation in the macro body outside quote does not; the use documentation rule needs the effects of use in an admonition at the top of @moduledoc, and prose or nothing is violated; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden in all five runs); a block that would fit as a do: line is a judgement call that decides no verdict; `unless` is listed under the branching rule, `if ... else` validation is not; a one-line multi-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; a catch-all public match clause or an unguarded match/1 is listed under Make polymorphism explicit; a format failure whose only change is parentheses on the two get calls is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens. The other changes since 3e3581d (the routing-table row and testing.md renamed to references/ex_unit.md with a reworded Assert with patterns, the Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, step 1 of Before you finish) touch no rule in macro-dsl's index list; the named-argument rule's new sentence "That holds whether the result is passed on, matched against, nested in another call or discarded." is the basis for the one other_violations entry under it (haiku-2's inline multi-line raise CompileError options).

Changed rule, graded against its current text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability): Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. Since 3e3581d the two clause-consistency sentences ("A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line. When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.") are replaced by "A function may mix the forms: a short clause on `do:`, a clause that needs a block as a block, each block clause set apart with a blank line." That sentence is broken by no run: the mixed functions (haiku-1 bind/3 lines 84-94; haiku-2 bind/3 lines 74-84 and validate_path!/2 lines 86-93; sonnet-1 match_route/2 lines 80-87; sonnet-2 validate_handler!/1 lines 112-119) set every block clause apart; opus-1's validate_path!/1 is three blocks this time. opus-1 and sonnet-2 splice generated clauses with unquote_splicing(clauses) directly above a do: catch-all (opus-1 lines 73-74, whose spliced clauses are blocks written at lines 93-97 in match_clause/1); the block clauses are not written at that spot, so this is not counted. The deciding sentence this sweep is the unchanged "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line: when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`, so write a block or move part of the body into a helper.": 2 of 5, sonnet-1 (lines 91-92 and 94-95, written wrapped by the session, 146 and 131 characters joined, no guard) and sonnet-2 (line 54, 100 characters inside the quote, which mix format wraps; no guard). sonnet-2 lines 112-113 are a head broken after a long guard (106 characters joined), the one wrap the rule keeps. "Use `do:` for a body of one expression": 0 (every one-expression block was joined and measured at 102 to 138 characters except opus-1's generated clause at lines 94-96, 97 characters, a judgement call). "The same holds for `if`": 0; no run writes `if ..., do:` and every if or unless block would run past 98 characters as a do: form. Any sentence: 2 of 5, so Opus clean, Haiku clean, Sonnet violated (2026-10-22-c baseline: all three tiers violated).

Compile-time dependencies were checked with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects, one per run, with the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex (so xref line numbers match the run file) and real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/my_app/handlers.ex. Every run reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (compile) on the two get lines; all five call Macro.expand on the handler (opus-1 line 128, haiku-1 line 36, haiku-2 line 96, sonnet-1 line 33, sonnet-2 line 37).

Bad-declaration checks: each run's project was loaded, then Code.compile_string compiled one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All ten fail while get expands in the router module: ArgumentError in opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-2, CompileError in haiku-2 and sonnet-1.

Format: mix format on copies adds parentheses to the two get calls in all five runs (result.json format_ok is false for that reason); it also reflows opus-1 line 114, haiku-2 line 92 and sonnet-2 line 54, which are listed under Before you finish (sonnet-2's also under the do: rule). haiku-1's and sonnet-1's only change is the get parentheses (sonnet-1's wrapped do: lines are kept by the formatter as written). All five compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors.

Reads: result.json reads is empty for all five runs; the transcripts never mention SKILL.md, macros.md or library-design.md and make no Skill call, as the baseline prompt's last line asks. The Expected reads line is missed by design in every run.

Smoke test outside the rules: all five return the routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/" with string param keys, and return :error for "/nope". match(123) raises FunctionClauseError in the generated match/1 in opus-1 and haiku-2, raises FunctionClauseError in String.split/3 in haiku-1 (unguarded match/1), and returns :error in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 (catch-all clauses). opus-1 and sonnet-2 build pattern variables with String.to_atom from the route string, which is source code, not external input, so it is not counted under the atom rule.

Against 2026-10-22-c baseline: opus-1 now specs the generated routes/0 and match/1, so the opus tier moves from violated to clean on the spec rule, and writes validate_path!/1 as three blocks, so it moves from violated to clean on the do: rule; the haiku tier moves from violated to clean on the do: rule (no 99-character bind/3 line this time); sonnet-1 now specs routes/0 and match/1 but leaves its @doc false helpers unspecced. Every run this sweep again has the direct-attribute-write shape, no admonition, and compile-time handler dependencies through Macro.expand; Write a function unless the job needs a macro, Unquote each argument once and Write module names literally stay clean in all five.
